title: Chapter 125 — First Contact & Greetings
intro: The first 10 seconds set the tone for the entire relationship.

sections.title: The 10-Second Window
sections.content:
Whether a customer walks in, calls, or emails — how you open determines whether they feel welcomed or processed. You have about 10 seconds to make eye contact, smile, and acknowledge them.

In-store: make eye contact within 10 seconds. Walk toward them. Introduce yourself by name. Do NOT ask 'can I help you' — use 'Welcome in, I am [name]. What brings you in today?'

On the phone: answer within 3 rings. 'Thank you for calling [store], this is [name]. How can I help you?' Warm, professional, and personal.

sections.title: Reading Body Language
sections.content:
Browsers walk slowly and look around without focus. Researchers walk directly to a specific area and check their phone. Urgent buyers walk fast and look for the nearest rep. Couples signal through their body positioning — who is leading, who is hesitating.

Match your approach to their energy. The browser needs space and a gentle invitation. The researcher needs to be acknowledged as informed. The urgent buyer needs speed. Read the room before you open your mouth.

sections.title: Avoiding the 'Just Looking' Trigger
sections.content:
'Can I help you?' triggers 'just looking' 80 percent of the time. It is a closed question that invites a closed answer.

Better approaches: 'Are you working on a project or just getting ideas?' gives them permission either way. 'What brings you in today?' opens a conversation. 'I see you are looking at dishwashers — are you replacing one or doing a kitchen project?' shows you are paying attention.

The goal is engagement, not interrogation. Make them feel welcome, not watched.
